evidence.text: A land with your Presence is **your land**. Your **Sacred Site** is a land with **two or more of your Presence**, not one disk each from different Spirits. Three or more still count as only one Sacred Site there. Any number of Spirits and disks can share a land. Explicit special rules such as River's Domain can create Sacred Sites differently, without adding imaginary Presence disks. Presence actions normally affect disks on the island, never track disks, unless stated otherwise.

answers.answer: Choke the Land with Green is optional despite printings omitting “may.” Steady Regeneration tests whether the Blight Card is Healthy/Blighted, not Blight in the destination. Growth instructions from multiple options can be ordered together, so a gained Power can inform the mandatory placement.

evidence.text: - **A Spread of Rampant Green:** **Choke the Land with Green** is optional (some printings omit “may”). Each use skips just that Ravage or Build action and costs one of Green's Presence in its Sacred Site there. A later Build needs a fresh decision and another disk: starting with three, Green may skip the Ravage, retain a two-disk Sacred Site, then skip the Build and end with one disk. **Steady Regeneration**'s Healthy/Blighted test refers to the Blight Card, not Blight in the destination land. When adding Presence via Growth, Green may use destroyed disks instead of track disks even while disks remain on tracks: this is free while Healthy, or costs 1 Energy per destroyed disk while Blighted. This permission applies only to Growth; an ordinary Power needs its own explicit destroyed-Presence permission. Green's separate **Always** Range-2 Jungle/Wetland placement is additional to its one chosen Growth group, including when it chooses Reclaim/gain a Power. It still chooses only one of the optional groups. Growth instructions from multiple options can be ordered together, so a gained Power may inform the mandatory placement. Its explicit regeneration can use destroyed Presence; ordinary placement cannot. [Core: .9v5kc2v, .7w4g8r1, .bu6oegz, .7w4g8nv]

answers.answer: Yes, a Power may Push Invaders into that board’s Ocean and Ocean Drowns them if Ocean has Presence anywhere on that board; it need not be in the Ocean. Fear Cards and Invader actions do not ordinarily treat Ocean as a land.

evidence.text: Each balanced board has eight lands, two each of Jungle, Mountain, Sands and Wetland. Lands are adjacent if they touch by border **or corner**, including across boards. Ocean is not normally a land or in play. Only lands touching a printed Ocean are Coastal; the other outside edges are cliffs, not coast. Other lands are Inland.

answers.answer: Blight can cascade into Ocean on a board with Ocean’s Presence. Ordinary Growth cannot Add Presence there merely by treating it as Coastal Wetland, though it may measure Range from existing Ocean Presence. Ocean’s explicit “any Ocean” Growth group places Presence only in an Ocean; for Inland Presence, it needs an explicit permission such as Indomitable Claim.

evidence.text: - **Ocean's Hungry Grasp:** On a board with any of Ocean's Presence, the Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for **Powers and Blight**, not for normal Growth, Invader actions or Fear Cards. Powers and Special Rules can measure Range through it as a land. [Core: range-through-ocean] Powers can target it and move Invaders/Dahan into it; Blight can cascade into it. Other Spirits' Presence may end up there via a legal Power, including Thunderspeaker accompanying moved Dahan. You can measure Growth placement Range **from existing Ocean Presence**, although normal Growth cannot add to the Ocean just by treating it as a Coastal Wetland. The Growth group explicitly adding two Presence in **any Ocean** can place them in any board's Ocean, even a board where Ocean has no Presence, without a numeric Range requirement. This Growth group places in Oceans only; it does not place Presence Inland. Its other group's Range-1 **Coastal land** placement does not permit placing in the Ocean. Other placement must respect Ocean's land-type restriction unless expressly ignored (e.g., **Indomitable Claim** for Inland Presence).
